sections.name: Wanted level one star (police)
sections.card:
Summary: Of all six levels, only one star keeps the police from using firearms; they try to arrest you instead.
Weak points: You can lose them by leaving the search circle, which is about two city blocks across at one star, and staying out of it for several seconds: the police then give up and the wanted level goes away. Their cars chase at a moderate speed and try to box you in rather than ram you.
Tips: One star comes from minor things such as attacking civilians, damaging a vehicle, stealing a car in sight of police or passing a toll booth without paying. On foot you can resist arrest, but that jumps you to two stars and the police start shooting; keeping a one-star level for a while also leads to two stars.

sections.name: Wanted level two stars (police shotguns)
sections.card:
Summary: Two stars is where the police start using firearms, and pump shotguns may be among them; in a chase they try to pull ahead of you or push you off the road.
Danger: More police cars are sent, and the fit officers riding up front climb out with pump shotguns. If you crash, they try to hem you in with their cars.
Tips: Two stars come from firing a gun or setting off an explosion near an officer, punching an officer again and again, killing many people quickly, wrecking a gas station's fuel pump or a Gruppe 6 Securicar, and resisting arrest.

sections.name: Wanted level three stars (NOOSE, Police Maverick)
sections.card:
Summary: At three stars NOOSE steps in with Cruisers and Patriots, putting roadblocks across main roads and bridges, and the Patriots try to ram you head-on. A Police Maverick also joins, lighting you up with a spotlight at night and shooting as soon as its officers have a clear line.
Weak points: The helicopter breaks off the chase every so often if you drop underground, shelter in a big structure for a long while, or kill both of its riflemen.
Tips: From three stars you can no longer board the subway, and Police Predator patrol boats are sent if you are in or near water. Three stars come from killing or wounding an officer with a gun, or from carrying on with the damage and fighting back at the police.

sections.name: Wanted level four stars (FIB, NOOSE Tactical Response Unit)
sections.card:
Summary: Four stars sends the FIB or NOOSE's Tactical Response Unit after you, four officers to a vehicle, in Enforcer armored vans or FIB Buffalo sedans. The search area is now roughly the size of Bohan.
Danger: Most carry carbine rifles, a few have SMGs or pump shotguns, and their body armor lets them soak up more gunfire before they drop.
Tips: They can take around 30 seconds to arrive. Driving fast or switching vehicles all the time seems to make the FIB more likely to turn up. Four stars also come from going onto the runway at Francis International Airport or into the Civilization Committee grounds in Algonquin.

sections.name: Wanted level five and six stars (Annihilators, snipers)
sections.card:
Summary: At five stars two NOOSE Annihilator helicopters replace the Police Mavericks, and in the main game every officer fires on you while chasing.
Danger: Officers drive harder, using the PIT maneuver to spin you out. FIB and NOOSE units turn up in equal numbers, and where there are tall buildings, officers with Combat Sniper rifles shoot at you whenever they can see you.
Weak points: An Annihilator takes a lot of damage from RPGs, assault rifles and other Annihilators, and one rocket straight into its fuselage can destroy it.
Tips: At six stars the search area covers roughly the borough of Broker and Dukes. No military units are sent, and officers with PSG-1 sniper rifles keep spawning.

sections.name: Police Maverick
sections.card:
Summary: Three stars brings a Police Maverick with a pilot and two riflemen aboard. The riflemen carry carbine rifles and open fire as soon as they see you.
Weak points: The cockpit is open to fire, so the officers in front can be hit from tall places or with assault rifles. When the helicopter passes over you, its lower windows may be a weak spot too.
Tips: At four stars NOOSE crew replace the officers aboard if NOOSE is sent, and from five stars an Annihilator can replace the helicopter. Shooting the pilot lets it drift down undamaged about half the time; otherwise it spins and explodes.

sections.name: Yardies
sections.card:
Summary: Jamaican posses that act as one loose group. You will meet them mostly around Beechwood City in Broker, and less in Schottler and Willis. Their cars are painted green, black and gold, like the Jamaican flag.
Weapons: Street members carry pistols, Micro SMGs and pump shotguns, and are well armed.
Tips: Attack them before the mission Shadow and they turn hostile. They welcome you onto their turf, and once Shadow is done they defend you if you get into a fight or a pedestrian attacks you.

sections.name: Spanish Lords
sections.card:
Summary: A Puerto Rican gang and one of the biggest street gangs in the game. They hold South Bohan, Cerveza Heights, East Holland and Alderney City, plus Fortside but only at night, and dress in black and gold or red and blue.
Weapons: At night expect Micro SMGs and pistols. Hit a car with one of them inside and he may get out holding a knife.
Tips: In Alderney City they share turf with the Korean Mob and do not fight each other; they sometimes ride in the same car, and both attack you if that car is damaged, and they turn on each other if you start a shoot-out.

sections.name: Body Armor
sections.card:
Summary: Body armor is a blue vest. It appears on screen as a blue half-circle meter beside the radar, next to the green health meter. When you aim at a target wearing armor, usually a NOOSE or FIB agent, a small light blue circle shows by the reticle.
Uses: It soaks up gunfire, explosions and fire so your health lasts longer. It does not protect you from falls, from being hit by a vehicle on foot, or from melee attacks.
Where to get it: The underground gun shops sell it for $500 once the mission Do You Have Protection? is done. It also lies around the city with a red glow, and an Enforcer van gives you only about a third of a full vest.

sections.name: Health packs and food
sections.card:
Summary: Health packs look like medical kits and are scattered across Liberty City: mostly in quiet corners, and also in hospitals and subway stations.
Uses: Food from Cluckin' Bell, Burger Shot, street vendors or vending machines puts health back by varying amounts, and drinks usually give back less.
Tips: Dial 911, then 2, to call an ambulance; the paramedics restore your health and charge up to $950, depending on how hurt you are. You cannot raise your maximum health in GTA IV, and saving the game also refills it.

sections.name: Underground Gun Shops
sections.card:
Summary: Three underground gun shops stand in Downtown Broker, Chinatown in Algonquin and Port Tudor in Alderney, and they open with the mission Do You Have Protection?.
Uses: You walk up to a table to look at a gun; ammo costs less than the gun, and the stock grows as the story goes on. A Pistol costs $600, a Pump Shotgun or Micro SMG $1,200, and an Assault Rifle $3,500.
Tips: You cannot enter with a wanted level, because the door stays locked. Do not shoot the clerk: guards loitering at the entrance defend the shop, and if you kill the owner they attack with Combat Shotguns and SMGs and the shop will not sell to you for a while.

sections.name: Car Bomb
sections.card:
Summary: Four blocks of explosive with a phone wired to them, planted under a vehicle and set off by calling Packie and choosing Detonate.
Uses: Setting it off gives you no wanted level, which makes it a handy way to destroy Securicars.
Tips: Packie sends car bombs to wherever you are as a friend favor. The bombs can only be planted under a car, a bus or a light van.

sections.name: RPG
sections.card:
Summary: Nothing else in the game is as powerful. One direct hit destroys any target, and the blast also hurts everyone close by.
Uses: You aim over the shoulder, so you can strafe and shoot from behind cover. The rocket blows up by itself at its maximum range, and it glances off a solid surface if it meets it at roughly 25 degrees.
Tips: Once you finish the mission Babysitting, the underground gun shops sell the RPG at $15,000, and each extra rocket costs another $5,000. The simplest one to grab is on a big rock in the water north of Northwood. A helicopter does not need a direct hit: the blast can make the pilot lose control and crash.

sections.name: Molotov Cocktail
sections.card:
Summary: A thrown bottle of Cherenkov Vodka that sets things on fire, and the only fire-based weapon you can use.
Uses: One bottle sets an enemy on fire and drops him for a short time, and a second can burn him to death; armored NOOSE and FIB agents may need a third, because body armor suppresses the fire.
Tips: Underground gun shops sell them for $500 after the mission The Master and the Molotov. From a car it is hard to use, as the bottle has to hit the target directly, but four bottles set a car ablaze and six destroy it or leave it unusable.

sections.name: Grenade
sections.card:
Summary: A thrown grenade you can drop at your feet, hold to cook before throwing, or throw back; if you hold it too long it beeps and then explodes in your hand.
Uses: In GTA IV your own grenades are far deadlier to you than to enemies. An enemy will most likely survive unless the grenade lands very close, and enemies run clear of one that is about to explode.
Tips: Dropped from a moving car they beat Molotov Cocktails, because of their far larger blast, but keep driving so your own car is not caught. The underground gun shops sell them for $1,000 after the mission Deconstruction for Beginners.
